items.title: John Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 18, 2023 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: INTERVIEWER mentions Bach in the context of the song 'Time and Love' using Bach's chords; Interviewee does not mention Bach directly, only responding to the interviewer's statement.

ctx.x: mentioned that Sebesky record a number of times in other interviews I was looking at today. And Sebesky was a big part of my life in the ‘90s and well just from the ‘90s all the way ‘til his passing. You know somebody like Don Sebesky, you know, writing these arrangements and then you start to see how he harmonizes stuff and you go oh yeah that was cool. So when you start to write the chords out for somebody you go what would Don have done here? You know that was a gift.

Yeah that “Time and Love” song, it took me a long time to realize besides using the melody from the Bach, he pretty much used the chart. He used Bach’s chords and wrote that beautiful thing. It just — every time it really gets to me.

And there’s “Afternoon of a Faun” and “Lazy Afternoon” on that record. My manager back then, Buddy Morra in the ‘90s was friends with Don and he always would say to me, “You know you’ve got to get Don to give you that chart because Jessica could sing that thing and oh it’s so good.” But it’s amazing to have been with all those people and all the people that they wrote for and the stories that they had to tell. So that’s what you’re doing.
